method: D(t) = A(t) - B(t), the difference of the two regions' deseasonalized fixed-mask monthly means on the months where both have a value; Sen's slope with 95% CI and Mann-Kendall (same autocorrelation handling as the regional trends) on D. 'trends differ' when p < alpha. P-values of the two regions are never compared, and overlapping confidence intervals are not used as a test. When the boxes overlap, the shared cells do not cancel in D: each mean is divided by its own total area weight (W_A, W_B), so a shared cell i enters D with weight w_i (1/W_A - 1/W_B), which is zero only when W_A = W_B.
note: Each p-value is valid for one comparison chosen in advance. Looking through many pairs and picking those that differ raises the chance of false positives: about 1 in 20 pairs with no real difference will show 'trends differ'. When two boxes overlap, their averages share data and the two results are not independent. Shared cells do not fully cancel in the difference, because each average is divided by its own area, so read such a result as a comparison of two overlapping areas.
